summary: 9remote exposes a remote-controlled PTY shell on the installer's host via Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
details: On startup, the package binds a local HTTP/socket.io server on port 2208 and opens a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel via a bundled cloudflared, exposing the host to inbound connections that bypass local NAT/firewall. Messages received over the network are forwarded through a UNIX-socket daemon (ptyDaemon.cjs) into node-pty shells (bash/zsh/sh on Unix; cmd/powershell/pwsh on Windows), where `input` messages are written directly to the PTY via `b.pty.write(r.data)`. A remote party who obtains the 30-minute QR pairing key gains an interactive shell on the installer's machine with the privileges of the user running the tool, i.e. full-host remote code execution. The postinstall script also installs an auxiliary package (systray2@2.1.4, pinned) into ~/.9remote/runtime/node_modules and chmods the tray binary to 0755; this part is aggressive but publisher-controlled and version-pinned.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
